question: In CKD G4–G5, dietary potassium restriction is recommended to prevent hyperkalaemia because the kidneys lose their ability to excrete excess potassium as nephron mass falls.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Potassium excretion is impaired in advanced CKD (G4–G5) as nephron mass falls. Dietary potassium restriction (≤2–3 g/day) helps prevent hyperkalaemia. This is a core component of CKD supportive dietary management alongside phosphate and protein restriction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. As eGFR falls below 20–30 mL/min (G4–G5), the remaining nephrons cannot maintain potassium homeostasis. Dietary potassium restriction (typically ≤2–3 g/day) is recommended, along with phosphate restriction and protein restriction (0.6–0.8 g/kg/day in non-dialysis CKD). Hyperkalaemia in CKD is a major cause of life-threatening arrhythmia.
